author: Nordmann, 1835
status: 나그네새, 해마다 수십 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
summary: 봄과 가을에 적은 수가 서해안 일대를 지나가는 매우 드문 나그네새로, 해안 갯벌이나 강 하구에 내려앉는다. 재빨리 달려가 게를 잡아먹으며, 갑각류, 어류, 연체동물 등을 먹는다. 알은 4개쯤 낳는데, 청록색 바탕에 검은 갈색 반점이 있다. 국내에서는 서해안과 남해안에서 관찰되고, 세계적으로는 사할린에 분포한다.

art.subject: Nordmann's Greenshank (Tringa guttifer), adult in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean west-coast mudflats in late April and May: crown and hindneck white, densely streaked and spotted black; face whitish with fine dark streaks; mantle, scapulars and tertials blackish with small whitish notches and pale fringes, so the upperparts look dark and scaly; lower neck and breast white with bold, rounded black spots forming a broad spotted band, a few spots on the flanks; belly and undertail white. Bill thick-based and slightly upturned, dull yellowish on the basal half and blackish on the outer half; dark eye; legs yellow.
art.pose: running quickly across a tidal mudflat to catch a crab
art.scene: Korean west-coast tidal mudflat at a river mouth during spring migration; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding plumage (late April–May), side view standing: blackish scaly upperparts with white notches, white head and neck densely streaked black, bold round black spots across the breast, white belly, thick slightly upturned bill with a yellowish basal half, short yellow legs

adult winter plumage, side view standing: pale grey upperparts with narrow whitish fringes, head and neck only faintly streaked grey, very white face and underparts, dark-tipped bill with a yellowish base, short greenish-yellow legs
in flight, seen from below: clean white underwing coverts and white body, pale tail, only the toes projecting just beyond the tail tip
art.build: Medium-large, stocky Tringa sandpiper, 29–32cm, about the size of a Common Greenshank but heavier-chested, shorter-necked and noticeably shorter-legged, so it looks low-slung and often crouches as it runs after crabs. Bill thick at the base, a little longer than the head, straight for most of its length with a slight upward tilt towards the tip. Legs yellow and relatively short; the front toes are partly webbed. In flight a white wedge runs from the rump up the back, the tail is pale with faint barring, the underwing coverts are clean white, and only the toes project slightly beyond the tail tip.
avoid: Do not paint the long slim legs, slimmer bill and finely streaked breast of Common Greenshank (Tringa nebularia); Nordmann's is shorter-legged and thicker-billed with round black breast spots.
Do not let the legs trail far behind the tail in flight; only the toes project slightly.
Do not paint grey-barred underwing coverts; they are white.
Do not paint red or orange legs (Spotted Redshank, Common Redshank, Terek Sandpiper).
Do not make the bill strongly upcurved like an avocet's; the upturn is slight.
